name: Question 1
problem: Find $∠BAC$ given the points $A(1,0,-2)$, $B(1,2,4)$, and $C(3,-2,1).$ Round your answer to the nearest degree.
worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A$, $B$, $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨1,0,-2⟩,\,b=⟨1,2,4⟩,\,c=⟨3,-2,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠BAC=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13978202/assets/285b8343208079181ac6036cf9ca16abc974d59b9262878ed40c0da9af5683d0.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =⟨1,2,4⟩-⟨1,0,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨0,2,6⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =⟨3,-2,1⟩-⟨1,0,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-2,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{0\cdot 2+2\cdot (-2)+6\cdot 3}{\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{6}^{2}}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{14}{\sqrt{40}\cdot \sqrt{17}} \\  & =\frac{7}{\sqrt{170}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{7}{\sqrt{170}})≈{58}^{∘}.
$$

Correct
EXPLANATION

Note that the position vectors of the points A, B, C are

a=⟨1,0,−2⟩,b=⟨1,2,4⟩,c=⟨3,−2,1⟩.

The triangle △ABC is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote ∠BAC=θ.

First, we find the components of AB→ and AC→:

AB→=b−a=⟨1,2,4⟩−⟨1,0,−2⟩=⟨0,2,6⟩AC→=c−a=⟨3,−2,1⟩−⟨1,0,−2⟩=⟨2,−2,3⟩

Now, the cosine of the angle between AB→ and AC→ is

cos⁡θ=AB→⋅AC→|AB→||AC→|=0⋅2+2⋅(−2)+6⋅302+22+6222+(−2)2+32=1440⋅17=7170.

Hence, θ=arccos⁡(7170)≈58∘.
